scope: All pinned C/H deinit references scanned, followed by exact function inspection
findings: MBSS_Close stops the netdev queue, kicks associated stations, disables beacon request and refreshes beacon configuration; it does not deinit/free BeaconPkt.
MBSS_Remove deinitializes each virtual BSS beacon before detach/unregister/free of its netdev.
The rt_profile.c call targets MAIN_MBSSID during adapter teardown, not ordinary ra2 virtual close.
wdev_bcn_buf_deinit requires IDLE in the original MT path then marks STOP and frees BeaconPkt. Isolated candidate adds stricter drain/locking guards; this audit does not bypass them.
conclusion: Existing virtual-close lifetime supports retaining the mapped beacon packet object across ordinary OFF/ON. This does not establish the DMA mapping, RF queue or late-TxS boundary.
remaining: Trace APMakeAllBssBeacon and virtual-open rebuild ownership in the final composed candidate
Bind reservation-free mode only with periodic pacing and producer/registration checks
Retain physical remove/adapter shutdown guards separately
scratch: Read existing archive in place; no source extraction retained
